# PETadex.v260701 Creation: 2. Searching Plasticome.v2 against nr

> **Author:** Thomas Quigley\
> **Date Started:** July 16th, 2026\
> **Date Finished:** August 21st, 2026\
> **Input:** s3://petadex/petadex.v260701/1_pazy_cleaning/petadex-plasticome.v260701.90pid-centroids.fastaa\
> **Output:** \
> s3://petadex/petadex.v260701/2_nr_search/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.fastaa \
> s3://petadex/petadex.v260701/2_nr_search/petadex-plasticome.v260701.proteins.fastaa

---

## 1. Objective

The goal of this notebook is to retrieve a set of plastic-degrading enzyme homologs from the NCBI non-redundant protein database. When someone studies a protein and obtains it's amino acid sequence, they give this sequence to the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI). NCBI then adds this sequence to it's database, which is the NCBI nr protein database. If this amino acid sequence has already been added to the database before, the sequence is not added again (hence non-redundant), but the newly added accession and it's corresponding sequence metadata (from the researcher) is appended to the sequence information. The goal is to search through this database and retrieve as many homologs to plastic-degrading enzymes as possible.

The search will be performed by DIAMOND sequence alignment, and will query the 90pid centroids from Plasticome.v2 against the NCBI nr database. The target hits will then be deduplicated (some accessions can hit to multiple query sequences), and subsetted to significant hits based on an e-value cutoff of 1.0e-5. To ensure that Plasticome.v2 and the PETadex-nr datasets are non-redundant to each other (Plasticome sequences exist in nr), all sequences from nr that have a plasticome accession will be removed from the significant hits file.

**NOTE: By ensuring that the datasets (petadex-nr and petadex-plasticome) are non-redundant to each other, this ensures that the dataset is clustered at 100.0%. Therefore the definition of a protein is 100.0% centroids.**

### 1.1. Place in the Project
---
We want to discover all homologs of PETadex-Plasticome.v260701 in NCBI nr to create the seed query against Logan to retrieve all homologs of homologs of plastic-degrading enzymes. The returned dataset of hits will need to be further quality controlled using HMMs to ensure that the correct catalytic domains are hit.

## 2. Experiment
### 2.0. Install requirements and diamond database set up
---
1. ncbi-blast-2.17.0+
2. DIAMOND version 2.2.4

For this script, we have NCBI BLAST nr already downloaded to the server, which is an indexed database ready for a blast search. We can then convert this to a DIAMOND database with the following script:


```bash
%%bash

# ────────────────────────────────── #
# SETTING UP THE DIAMOND NR DATABASE #
# ────────────────────────────────── #

# ─── INPUT ─── #
NCBI_NR_SOURCE="/watson/rnalab/shared/nr/nr" # this is the source NCBI BLAST nr indexed database

# ─── WORKING ─── #
NCBI_NR_DATASET="./2_nr_search/input/ncbi-blast_nr-2.17.0+.fastaa" # this is where the 300 GB of NCBI nr sequences will go

# ─── LOGS ─── #
BLASTDBCMD_LOG="./2_nr_search/logs/petadex-nr.v260701.blastdbcmd.log" # this is the log file for extracting the NCBI sequences, will be blank if it works
MAKEDB_LOG="./2_nr_search/logs/petadex-nr.v260701.makedb.log" # this is the log for making the DIAMOND database

# ─── OUTPUT ─── #
DIAMOND_NR_DATABASE="./2_nr_search/input/ncbi-blast_nr-2.17.0+.dmnd" # this is where the 500 GB DIAMOND database file will go

# ─── CREATING THE NR FASTAA FROM A BLAST DB ─── #
echo "# ============================================================ #"
echo "# Coping the sequences from the NCBI-BLAST-2.17.0+ to a fastaa #"
echo "# ============================================================ #"

blastdbcmd -db "${NCBI_NR_SOURCE}" -dbtype prot -entry all -out "${NCBI_NR_DATASET}" > "${BLASTDBCMD_LOG}" 2>&1
cat "${BLASTDBCMD_LOG}"

# ─── CREATING THE DIAMOND DB ─── #
echo "# =========================== #"
echo "# Creating a diamond database #"
echo "# =========================== #"

diamond makedb --in "${NCBI_NR_DATASET}" -d "${DIAMOND_NR_DATABASE}" --threads 200 > "${MAKEDB_LOG}" 2>&1
cat "${MAKEDB_LOG}"
```

### 2.1. Search our validated plastic-degrading enzymes against NCBI nr
---
This section will take the fastaa file of Plasticome.v2 90pid centroid sequences and query them against NCBI nr. The options were selected with the following reasons:
- --outfmt 6: Includes a comprehensive list of results that will be parsed
- --very-sensitive: Will search for things that are &lt;40pid, the "twilight zone"
- -k0: Allows unlimited hits


```bash
%%bash

# ───────────────────────────────────── #
# SEARCH PLASTICOME.V2 AGAINST NCBI NR  #
# ───────────────────────────────────── #

# ─── INPUT ─── #
PLASTICOME_V2_FASTAA="../s3/1_pazy_cleaning/petadex-plasticome.v260701.90pid-centroids.fastaa"
DIAMOND_NR_DATABASE="./2_nr_search/input/ncbi-blast_nr-2.17.0+.dmnd"

# ─── OUTPUT ─── #
NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH_V2="../s3/2_nr_search/petadex-nr.v260701.raw_hits.pro"

# ─── LOGS ─── #
DIAMOND_LOG_V2="./2_nr_search/logs/petadex-nr.v260701.raw_hits.log"

# ─── WORKING ─── #
TEMP_DIR="./2_nr_search/working/tmp"

# ─── PERFORM ALIGNMENT SEARCH ─── #
echo "Starting up Plasticome.v260701 Search..."
diamond blastp \
  -d "${DIAMOND_NR_DATABASE}" \
  -q "${PLASTICOME_V2_FASTAA}" \
  -o "${NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH_V2}" \
  --very-sensitive \
  -k0 \
  -b140 \
  -c1 \
  --threads 120 \
  --tmpdir "${TEMP_DIR}" \
  --outfmt 6 qseqid sseqid pident length mismatch gapopen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore \
  > "${DIAMOND_LOG_V2}" 2>&1
cat "${DIAMOND_LOG_V2}"
```

### 2.2. Parse the output of the DIAMOND search
---
This takes the TSV formatted DIAMOND output and keeps the lowest e-value hit for each non-redundant sequence (an amino acid sequence may have multiple genbank accessions). Any sequence that has an e-value hit below 1.0e-5 is written to the nr significant hits file, with the following header:

```
>genbank_accession:genbank_accession:ect|e_value|pid|bitscore|query_petadex_id|component_id
```

In order to visualize the dataset, the following plots are created before the e-value cutoff is applied (all are top e-value hit per sequence):
- A histogram of the e-value distributions.
- A scatterplot of the PID to e-value. **Note:** e-values of 0.0 are set to 1.0e-300 since the y-axis is logged. That's why there is a distinct line at 1.0e-300. That is not a bug.
- A barplot of the number of sequences that are above a given e-value cutoff (x-axis).


```python
# ───────────── #
# SCRIPT SET UP #
# ───────────── #
print("Starting up...")

import csv
import math
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ─── INPUT ─── #
NCBI_NR_DATASET="./2_nr_search/input/ncbi-blast_nr-2.17.0+.fastaa"

""" Format: has multiple accessions per sequence (hence non-redundant)
>WP_413685322.1 RNA-guided endonuclease InsQ/TnpB family protein [Proteus mirabilis] >XNR99298.1 transposase [Proteus mirabilis]
MKRLQAFKFQLRPNGQQEREMRRFAGACRFVFNRALARQNENYEAGNKYIPYTKMASWLIEWKSDTETQWLKEAPSQPLQ
QSLKDLERAYKNFFQQRTAFPRFKKRGKNDAFRYPQGVKLDQSNSRISLPKLGWMRYRNSREVVGEVRNVTVSQSCGKWY
"""

NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH="../s3/2_nr_search/petadex-nr.v260701.raw_hits.pro"

""" Format:
WP_116813002.1	WP_012460608.1	26.6	188	117	5	67	235	79	264	7.31e-04	54.3
"""
FIELDS = ["qseqid","sseqid","pident","length","mismatch","gapopen","qstart","qend","sstart","send","evalue","bitscore"]

# ─── OUTPUT FILES ─── #
NR_SIGNIFICANT_HITS = "./2_nr_search/working/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.plasticome-redundant.fastaa"

""" Format:
>genbank_accession:genbank_accession:ect|e_value|pid|bitscore|query_petadex_id|component_id
"""

EVALUE_HISTOGRAM_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.evalue_histogram.png"
SCATTER_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.pident_vs_evalue.png"
THRESHOLD_BARPLOT_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.evalue_threshold_barplot.png"

# ─── PARAMETERS ─── #
EVALUE_CUTOFF = 1.0e-5

# ─── PLOT COLOURS ─── #
BACKGROUND_COLOR = "#0f172a"
BIN_COLOR = "#dd3c3c"
EVALUE_BIN_COLOR = "#24ca5bff"
DOT_COLOR = "#ddb23c"
TEXT_COLOR = "#a1b0d4"
plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "sans-serif"
plt.rcParams["font.sans-serif"] = ["Arial", "Helvetica", "Nimbus Sans", "DejaVu Sans"]

# ────────────────────── #
# PARSING DIAMOND OUTPUT #
# ────────────────────── #

# ─── GET A LIST OF UNIQUE TARGET ACCESSIONS AND THEIR TOP HIT ─── #
n_total_hits = 0
target_accessions = set()
best_hit = {}  # sseqid -> (pident, evalue, qseqid, bitscore, length, qstart, qend, sstart, send) of the lowest-evalue hit
with open(NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH) as diamond_output:
    reader = csv.DictReader(diamond_output, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=FIELDS)
    for row in reader:
        n_total_hits += 1
        accession = row["sseqid"]
        pident = float(row["pident"])
        evalue = float(row["evalue"])
        bitscore = float(row["bitscore"])
        length = int(row["length"])
        qstart = int(row["qstart"])
        qend = int(row["qend"])
        sstart = int(row["sstart"])
        send = int(row["send"])
        query_sequence = row["qseqid"]
        target_accessions.add(accession)

        if accession not in best_hit or evalue < best_hit[accession][1]:
            best_hit[accession] = (pident, evalue, query_sequence, bitscore, length, qstart, qend, sstart, send)

print(f"Total hits in DIAMOND output: {n_total_hits:,}")
print(f"Unique target accessions:     {len(target_accessions):,}")

# ─── FASTAA READER ─── #
def iter_fasta(path):
    """
    Get (header_line, sequence) tuples from a fastaa file.
    """
    header = None
    seq_chunks = []
    with open(path) as fasta:
        for line in fasta:
            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            if line.startswith(">"):
                if header is not None:
                    yield header, "".join(seq_chunks)
                header = line
                seq_chunks = []
            else:
                seq_chunks.append(line)
        if header is not None:
            yield header, "".join(seq_chunks)

# ─────────────────────────────────── #
# RETRIEVE THE SEQUENCES FOR EACH HIT #
# ─────────────────────────────────── #
# the NCBI nr dataset groups identical 
# sequences under the same header, with all
# accessions listed (many > per header)

PROGRESS_EVERY = 100_000
n_processed = 0
n_matched = 0
n_below_cutoff = 0
plot_pidents = []
plot_evalues = []

with open(NR_SIGNIFICANT_HITS, "w") as raw_hits:
    for header, sequence in iter_fasta(NCBI_NR_DATASET):
        n_processed += 1
        if n_processed % PROGRESS_EVERY == 0:
            print(f"\rProcessed {n_processed:,} nr sequences | matched {n_matched:,}", end="", flush=True)

        # a single record's header can carry multiple ">accession description" entries
        accessions = [entry.split(maxsplit=1)[0] for entry in header[1:].split(">")]

        matched_accessions = [accession for accession in accessions if accession in target_accessions]
        if not matched_accessions:
            continue

        # of the diamond hits on this nr record, use the one with the lowest
        # e-value for the plot and the output header fields below
        pident, evalue, qseqid, bitscore, length, qstart, qend, sstart, send = min(
            (best_hit[accession] for accession in matched_accessions), key=lambda hit: hit[1]
        )
        plot_pidents.append(pident)
        plot_evalues.append(evalue)

        if evalue > EVALUE_CUTOFF:
            n_below_cutoff += 1
            continue

        qseqid_parts = qseqid.split("|")
        query_petadex_id = qseqid_parts[0]
        component_id = qseqid_parts[4] if len(qseqid_parts) >= 5 else ""

        raw_hits.write(
            f">{','.join(accessions)}|{evalue:.2e}|{pident}|{bitscore}|{query_petadex_id}|{component_id}\n{sequence}\n"
        )
        n_matched += 1

print(f"\rProcessed {n_processed:,} nr sequences | matched {n_matched:,} | below cutoff {n_below_cutoff:,}")
print(f"Remaining unique accessions:              {len(plot_pidents):,}")
print(f"Accessions passing e-value cutoff (<= {EVALUE_CUTOFF:g}): {n_matched:,} / {len(plot_pidents):,}")
print(f"Wrote {n_matched:,} matched sequences to {NR_SIGNIFICANT_HITS}")

# ───────────────────── #
# PLOT RAW DIAMOND HITS #
# ───────────────────── #

# ─── SHARED PLOT VARIABLES ─── #
safe_evalues = [evalue if evalue > 0 else 1e-300 for evalue in plot_evalues]

# ─── HISTOGRAM: TOP E-VALUE PER UNIQUE SEQUENCE ─── #
log_evalues = [math.log10(evalue) for evalue in safe_evalues]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
ax.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

ax.hist(log_evalues, bins=40, color=EVALUE_BIN_COLOR, edgecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

ax.set_xlabel("Top E-value to query (log10)", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax.set_ylabel("Unique target accessions", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax.set_title(f"Top E-value distribution ({len(plot_pidents):,} unique accessions)", color=TEXT_COLOR)

ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
    spine.set_alpha(0.4)

ax.grid(True, color=TEXT_COLOR, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(EVALUE_HISTOGRAM_OUT, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
plt.show()
print(f"Saved e-value histogram to {EVALUE_HISTOGRAM_OUT}")

# ─── SCATTER: PID VS. E-VALUE OF THE TOP E-VALUE HIT PER UNIQUE ACCESSION ─── #
fig2, ax2 = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
ax2.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

ax2.scatter(plot_pidents, safe_evalues, color=DOT_COLOR, s=12, alpha=0.7, edgecolor="none", zorder=3)
ax2.set_yscale("log")

ax2.set_xlabel("% identity of top e-value hit", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax2.set_ylabel("E-value", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax2.set_title(f"%Identity vs. E-value of top e-value hit ({len(plot_pidents):,} unique accessions)", color=TEXT_COLOR)

ax2.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)
for spine in ax2.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
    spine.set_alpha(0.4)

ax2.grid(True, color=TEXT_COLOR, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax2.set_axisbelow(True)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(SCATTER_OUT, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
plt.show()
print(f"Saved scatter plot to {SCATTER_OUT}")

# ─── BAR PLOT: UNIQUE ACCESSIONS BELOW E-VALUE THRESHOLDS ─── #
thresholds = [1e-5, 1e-10, 1e-15, 1e-20, 1e-25, 1e-30, 1e-100]
threshold_labels = ["E-5", "E-10", "E-15", "E-20", "E-25", "E-30", "E-100"]
threshold_counts = [sum(1 for e in plot_evalues if e < t) for t in thresholds]

fig3, ax3 = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
ax3.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

ax3.bar(threshold_labels, threshold_counts, color=BIN_COLOR, edgecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

ax3.set_xlabel("E-value threshold", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax3.set_ylabel("Unique target accessions", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax3.set_title(f"Unique sequences below e-value threshold ({len(plot_pidents):,} unique accessions)", color=TEXT_COLOR)

ax3.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)
for spine in ax3.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
    spine.set_alpha(0.4)

ax3.grid(True, axis="y", color=TEXT_COLOR, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax3.set_axisbelow(True)

for i, count in enumerate(threshold_counts):
    ax3.text(i, count, f"{count:,}", ha="center", va="bottom", color=TEXT_COLOR, fontsize=8)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(THRESHOLD_BARPLOT_OUT, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150)
plt.show()
print(f"Saved e-value threshold bar plot to {THRESHOLD_BARPLOT_OUT}")
```

### 2.2.1. Remove Plasticome accessions
---
We now have all the target hits from the DIAMOND search cleaned and parsed, except that some of the query sequences may some of the targets, since most Plasticome sequences are in NCBI nr. In this section, every sequence in the NR_SIGNIFICANT_HITS file will be cross-checked to Plasticome to see if either the accession or amino acid sequence is exactly the same. Remove all the matched Plasticome accessions from the nr hit dataset and create a new Plasticome-non-redundant fastaa. Any of the accessions that matched to Plasticome should be added to the header of the Plasticome sequence it matched to in the empty field of the input NON_REDUNDANT_PLASTICOME fastaa.


```python
# ───────────── #
# SCRIPT SET UP #
# ───────────── #
print("Starting up...")

import re

# ─── INPUT ─── #
NR_SIGNIFICANT_HITS = "./2_nr_search/working/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.plasticome-redundant.fastaa" # include some sequences that are in plasticome

NON_REDUNDANT_PLASTICOME= "../s3/1_pazy_cleaning/petadex-plasticome.v260701.100pid-centroids.fastaa"
"""
Header format:
>petadex_id|primary_accession| empty |pazy_id|component_id
ex.
>PL510|WOR09923.1|||C001
"""

# ─── OUTPUT ─── #
NR_CLEANED_TARGETS = "../s3/2_nr_search/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.fastaa" # removes any plasticome sequences

PLASTICOME_PROTEINS = "../s3/petadex-plasticome.v260701.proteins.fastaa" # primary accession cannot be found in matched_accessions field
"""
Header format:
>petadex_id|primary_accession|matched_accession_1:matched_accession_n|pazy_id|component_id
ex.
>PL510|WOR09923.1|||C001

For any
"""

# ───────────────────────────────────────── #
# LOAD THE NON-REDUNDANT PLASTICOME TARGETS #
# ───────────────────────────────────────── #

# ─── FASTAA READER ─── #
def iter_fasta(path):
    """
    Get (header_line, sequence) tuples from a fastaa file.
    """
    header = None
    seq_chunks = []
    with open(path) as fasta:
        for line in fasta:
            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            if line.startswith(">"):
                if header is not None:
                    yield header, "".join(seq_chunks)
                header = line
                seq_chunks = []
            else:
                seq_chunks.append(line)
        if header is not None:
            yield header, "".join(seq_chunks)

# ─── READ PLASTICOME ─── #
plasticome_headers = {}             # petadex_id -> header (without leading '>')
plasticome_sequences = {}           # petadex_id -> aa sequence
plasticome_accession_to_qseqid = {} # genbank_accession -> petadex_id
plasticome_sequence_to_qseqid = {}  # aa sequence -> petadex_id

for header, sequence in iter_fasta(NON_REDUNDANT_PLASTICOME):
    parts = header[1:].split("|")
    petadex_id = parts[0]
    plasticome_headers[petadex_id] = header[1:]
    plasticome_sequences[petadex_id] = sequence
    plasticome_sequence_to_qseqid[sequence] = petadex_id
    for accession in parts[1].split(":"):
        if accession:
            plasticome_accession_to_qseqid[accession] = petadex_id

n_plasticome_targets = len(plasticome_headers)
n_plasticome_accessions = len(plasticome_accession_to_qseqid)
print(f"Input Plasticome targets: {n_plasticome_targets:,} ({n_plasticome_accessions:,} with a known accession)")

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #
# CROSS-CHECK EVERY NR TARGET AGAINST PLASTICOME BY ACCESSION OR BY  #
# EXACT AMINO ACID SEQUENCE, REMOVING ANY MATCHES FROM THE NR OUTPUT #
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #

def correct_header(header, new_accessions):
    """
    Fill in the matched_accession field of a plasticome header with any newly
    discovered nr accessions, skipping ones already accounted for either as the
    primary accession or from an earlier nr hit on this petadex_id:
    >petadex_id|primary_accession|matched_accession_1:matched_accession_n|pazy_id|component_id
    """
    parts = header.split("|")
    plasticome_accessions = set(parts[1].split(":"))
    existing_matched = [accession for accession in parts[2].split(":") if accession]
    seen = plasticome_accessions | set(existing_matched)

    merged_matched = list(existing_matched)
    for accession in new_accessions:
        if accession not in seen:
            merged_matched.append(accession)
            seen.add(accession)

    parts[2] = ":".join(merged_matched)
    return "|".join(parts)

def petadex_sort_key(petadex_id):
    """
    Sort ascending by the numeric part of the petadex_id (e.g. PL2 before PL10),
    falling back to a plain string compare for anything that doesn't match.
    """
    match = re.match(r"[A-Za-z]*(\d+)", petadex_id)
    return (int(match.group(1)) if match else float("inf"), petadex_id)

# ─── READ NR ─── #
PROGRESS_EVERY = 100_000
n_input_targets = 0
n_matched = 0
n_kept = 0
plasticome_records = {}  # petadex_id -> (header, sequence), for entries updated during this pass

with open(NR_CLEANED_TARGETS, "w") as cleaned_out:
    for header, sequence in iter_fasta(NR_SIGNIFICANT_HITS):
        n_input_targets += 1
        if n_input_targets % PROGRESS_EVERY == 0:
            print(f"\rProcessed {n_input_targets:,} nr targets | matched {n_matched:,}", end="", flush=True)

        # accessions field can itself contain "|" characters from legacy NCBI
        # header formats, so split from the right for the 5 known trailing
        # fields instead of splitting on the first "|" in the header.
        accessions_field = header[1:].rsplit("|", 5)[0]
        accessions = accessions_field.split(",")

        matched_qseqids = {
            plasticome_accession_to_qseqid[accession]
            for accession in accessions
            if accession in plasticome_accession_to_qseqid
        }
        if sequence in plasticome_sequence_to_qseqid:
            matched_qseqids.add(plasticome_sequence_to_qseqid[sequence])

        if matched_qseqids:
            for qseqid in matched_qseqids:
                current_header, _ = plasticome_records.get(qseqid, (plasticome_headers[qseqid], plasticome_sequences[qseqid]))
                plasticome_records[qseqid] = (correct_header(current_header, accessions), sequence)
            n_matched += 1
            continue

        cleaned_out.write(f"{header}\n{sequence}\n")
        n_kept += 1

print(f"\rProcessed {n_input_targets:,} nr targets | matched {n_matched:,} | kept {n_kept:,}")
print(f"Input NR targets:                   {n_input_targets:,}")
print(f"Plasticome matches removed from nr:  {n_matched:,}")
print(f"Wrote {n_kept:,} cleaned nr sequences to {NR_CLEANED_TARGETS}")

# ─── FILL IN EVERY PLASTICOME TARGET THAT WASN'T MATCHED IN NR ─── #
n_query_matched = len(plasticome_records)
matched_petadex_ids = set(plasticome_records)
for petadex_id, header in plasticome_headers.items():
    if petadex_id not in plasticome_records:
        plasticome_records[petadex_id] = (header, plasticome_sequences[petadex_id])
n_query_unmatched = len(plasticome_records) - n_query_matched

# ─── WRITE THE PLASTICOME FASTAA, ASCENDING BY PETADEX_ID ─── #
with open(PLASTICOME_PROTEINS, "w") as plasticome_out:
    for petadex_id in sorted(plasticome_records, key=petadex_sort_key):
        plasticome_header, plasticome_sequence = plasticome_records[petadex_id]
        plasticome_out.write(f">{plasticome_header}\n{plasticome_sequence}\n")

print(f"Wrote {len(plasticome_records):,} plasticome sequences to {PLASTICOME_PROTEINS} ({n_query_matched:,} matched in nr, {n_query_unmatched:,} without a match)")

# ─── LOG KNOWN ACCESSIONS THAT NEVER MATCHED IN NR ─── #
known_accession_ids = set(plasticome_accession_to_qseqid.values())
unmatched_known_ids = sorted(known_accession_ids - matched_petadex_ids, key=petadex_sort_key)
print(f"Known accessions with no nr match: {len(unmatched_known_ids):,}")
for petadex_id in unmatched_known_ids:
    print(plasticome_headers[petadex_id])

```

### 2.3. Plot the e-value and PIDs per input query sequence, and count of targets per query
---
Using the output from the previous code block, I want to see what the distributions of pids and e-values are for all the significant hits for the entire dataset and for each query sequence. I additionally want to see how many target sequences there are per query sequence. How much of the database are homologs of just a few sequences?

The two repeated plots will be histograms of PID to query sequence and e-value.


```python
# ───────────── #
# SCRIPT SET UP #
# ───────────── #

print("Starting up...")

import csv
import os
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

import math
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

# ─── INPUT ─── #
NR_CLEANED_TARGETS = "../s3/2_nr_search/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.fastaa"
""" Format:
>genbank_accession:genbank_accession:ect|e_value|pid|bitscore|query_petadex_id|component_id
"""
#
PLASTICOME_V2_FASTAA = "../s3/1_pazy_cleaning/petadex-plasticome.v260701.90pid-centroids.fastaa"

# ─── OUTPUT ─── #
ALL_PID_HISTOGRAM = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.pid_histogram.png"
ALL_EVAL_HISTOGRAM = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.evalue_histogram.png"
PER_QUERY_COUNT_BARPLOT_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.per_query_count_barplot.png"
PER_QUERY_SHARE_PIE_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.per_query_share_pie.png"
COMPONENT_COUNT_BARPLOT_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.per_component_count_barplot.png"
COMPONENT_SHARE_PIE_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.per_component_share_pie.png"

PER_QUERY_PID_HISTOGRAM_DIR = "./2_nr_search/images/pid_per_query"
PER_QUERY_EVAL_HISTOGRAM_DIR = "./2_nr_search/images/eval_per_query"

# ─── PARAMETERS ─── #
TOP_N_QUERIES = 20  # number of individual slices in the per-query share pie chart, rest folds into "Other"

# ─── PLOT STYLE ─── #
BACKGROUND_COLOR = "#0f172a"
PID_BIN_COLOR = "#dd3c3c"
EVAL_BIN_COLOR = "#24ca5bff"
TEXT_COLOR = "#a1b0d4"
OTHER_SLICE_COLOR = "#64748b"  # for hits whose component isn't one of the top slices
plt.rcParams["font.family"] = "sans-serif"
plt.rcParams["font.sans-serif"] = ["Arial", "Helvetica", "Nimbus Sans", "DejaVu Sans"]


# ───────────────────────────── #
# PLOT SIGNIFICANT DIAMOND HITS #
# ───────────────────────────── #

# ─── SHARED COMPONENT -> COLOR MAPPING, USED BY EVERY PLOT BELOW ─── #
def build_categorical_palette(n):
    # tab20 + tab20b + tab20c gives 60 visually distinct swatches, matplotlib's
    # standard trick for coloring many categories
    swatches = list(plt.get_cmap("tab20").colors) + list(plt.get_cmap("tab20b").colors) + list(plt.get_cmap("tab20c").colors)
    return [swatches[i % len(swatches)] for i in range(n)]

# ─── CREATE PLOTTING FUNCTIONS ─── #
def plot_pid_histogram(pidents, title, out_path, show=False):
    """
    Plot the pid histogram
    """
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
    ax.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

    ax.hist(pidents, bins=40, color=PID_BIN_COLOR, edgecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

    ax.set_xlabel("% identity to query", color=TEXT_COLOR)
    ax.set_ylabel("Significant hits", color=TEXT_COLOR)
    ax.set_title(title, color=TEXT_COLOR)

    ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
        spine.set_alpha(0.4)

    ax.grid(True, color=TEXT_COLOR, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_path, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150)
    if show:
        plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)

def plot_eval_histogram(evalues, title, out_path, show=False):
    """
    Plot the e-value histogram

    Values of 0.0 are mapped to 1.0e-300
    so they can be plotted on a log exis
    """
    safe_evalues = [evalue if evalue > 0 else 1e-300 for evalue in evalues]
    log_evalues = [math.log10(evalue) for evalue in safe_evalues]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
    ax.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

    ax.hist(log_evalues, bins=40, color=EVAL_BIN_COLOR, edgecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, linewidth=0.5, zorder=3)

    ax.set_xlabel("E-value (log10)", color=TEXT_COLOR)
    ax.set_ylabel("Significant hits", color=TEXT_COLOR)
    ax.set_title(title, color=TEXT_COLOR)

    ax.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
        spine.set_alpha(0.4)

    ax.grid(True, color=TEXT_COLOR, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_path, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150)
    if show:
        plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)

def plot_share_pie(ranked_counts, top_n, label_for, title, out_path, color_for=None, other_color=OTHER_SLICE_COLOR):
    """
    Pie chart of the top_n largest categories by count, with the remainder
    folded into a single "Other" slice.

    color_for maps a category key to a fixed color (e.g. by component); if
    omitted, the top_n slices are colored from build_categorical_palette instead.
    """
    top_items = ranked_counts[:top_n]
    other_total = sum(count for key, count in ranked_counts[top_n:])
    n_other = len(ranked_counts) - len(top_items)

    pie_labels = [label_for(key) for key, count in top_items]
    pie_values = [count for key, count in top_items]
    pie_colors = [color_for(key) for key, count in top_items] if color_for else build_categorical_palette(len(top_items))

    if other_total:
        pie_labels.append(f"Other ({n_other:,} queries)")
        pie_values.append(other_total)
        pie_colors.append(other_color)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 9), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
    ax.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

    wedges, labels, autotexts = ax.pie(
        pie_values,
        labels=pie_labels,
        colors=pie_colors,
        autopct="%1.1f%%",
        pctdistance=0.78,
        startangle=90,
        counterclock=False,
        wedgeprops={"edgecolor": BACKGROUND_COLOR, "linewidth": 1.5},
        textprops={"color": TEXT_COLOR, "fontsize": 8},
    )
    for autotext in autotexts:
        autotext.set_color(BACKGROUND_COLOR)
        autotext.set_fontsize(7)
        autotext.set_fontweight("bold")

    ax.set_title(title, color=TEXT_COLOR)

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_path, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150)
    plt.show()
    print(f"Saved pie chart to {out_path}")

# ───────────────────────── #
# PARSE NR SIGNIFICANT HITS #
# ───────────────────────── #

# ─── READ FULL QUERY LIST (ALL 411 PLASTICOME.V2 QUERIES) ─── #
def iter_fasta_headers(path):
    with open(path) as fasta:
        for line in fasta:
            if line.startswith(">"):
                yield line.rstrip("\n")[1:]

all_query_ids = []
component_lookup = {}  # qseqid -> component_id, for every query, hit or not
for header in iter_fasta_headers(PLASTICOME_V2_FASTAA):
    parts = header.split("|")
    qseqid = parts[0]
    all_query_ids.append(qseqid)
    component_lookup[qseqid] = parts[4]

print(f"Total query sequences (Plasticome.v2 90pid centroids): {len(all_query_ids):,}")

# ─── READ SIGNIFICANT HITS HEADERS ─── #
def iter_headers(path):
    with open(path) as fasta:
        for line in fasta:
            if line.startswith(">"):
                yield line.rstrip("\n")[1:]

n_total_hits = 0
overall_pidents = []
overall_evalues = []
query_pidents = {qseqid: [] for qseqid in all_query_ids}  # qseqid -> [pident, pident, ...]
query_evalues = {qseqid: [] for qseqid in all_query_ids}  # qseqid -> [evalue, evalue, ...]

for header in iter_headers(NR_CLEANED_TARGETS):
    n_total_hits += 1
    if n_total_hits % 100_000 == 0:
        print(f"\rProcessed {n_total_hits:,} significant hits", end="", flush=True)

    # the accessions field (first field) can itself contain "|" characters from
    # legacy NCBI header formats (e.g. "prf||1301305A", "pir|B84556|"), so split
    # from the right for the 5 known trailing fields instead of splitting on
    # every "|" in the header.
    fields = header.rsplit("|", 5)
    evalue = float(fields[1])
    pident = float(fields[2])
    qseqid = fields[4]

    overall_pidents.append(pident)
    overall_evalues.append(evalue)
    query_pidents[qseqid].append(pident)
    query_evalues[qseqid].append(evalue)

print(f"\rProcessed {n_total_hits:,} significant hits")
n_queries_with_hits = sum(1 for pidents in query_pidents.values() if pidents)
zero_hit_queries = sorted(qseqid for qseqid, pidents in query_pidents.items() if not pidents)
print(f"Query sequences with a significant hit: {n_queries_with_hits:,} / {len(all_query_ids):,}")
if zero_hit_queries:
    print(f"Query sequences with zero significant hits ({len(zero_hit_queries):,}): {', '.join(zero_hit_queries)}")


sorted_components = sorted(set(component_lookup.values()))
component_color = dict(zip(sorted_components, build_categorical_palette(len(sorted_components))))
print(f"Unique components:      {len(sorted_components):,}")

# ────────────── #
# PLOT NR OUTPUT #
# ────────────── #
hit_counts = Counter({qseqid: len(pidents) for qseqid, pidents in query_pidents.items()})
ranked_hit_counts = hit_counts.most_common()  # [(qseqid, count), ...] descending by count

# ─── BAR PLOT: QUERY SEQUENCES PER COMPONENT ─── #
component_ordered_hits = sorted(
    hit_counts.items(), key=lambda item: (component_lookup.get(item[0], ""), -item[1])
)
ordered_counts = [count for qseqid, count in component_ordered_hits]
ordered_bar_colors = [component_color[component_lookup[qseqid]] for qseqid, count in component_ordered_hits]

GROUP_GAP = 1.5 # leave a gap between bars from different components so each component's group is visually separated
bar_positions = []
current_x = 0.0
previous_component = None
for qseqid, count in component_ordered_hits:
    component_id = component_lookup[qseqid]
    if previous_component is not None and component_id != previous_component:
        current_x += GROUP_GAP
    bar_positions.append(current_x)
    current_x += 1.0
    previous_component = component_id

fig4, ax4 = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 5.5), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
ax4.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

ax4.bar(bar_positions, ordered_counts, color=ordered_bar_colors, width=0.9, zorder=3)
ax4.set_yscale("log")
ax4.set_xlim(-1, bar_positions[-1] + 1)
ax4.set_xticks([])

ax4.set_xlabel("Query sequence (grouped by component, gap between components)", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax4.set_ylabel("Significant hits (log scale)", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax4.set_title(f"Significant hits per query sequence, grouped by component ({len(ordered_counts):,} query sequences)", color=TEXT_COLOR)

ax4.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)
for spine in ax4.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
    spine.set_alpha(0.4)

ax4.grid(True, axis="y", color=TEXT_COLOR, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax4.set_axisbelow(True)

component_legend_handles = [
    Patch(facecolor=component_color[component_id], edgecolor="none", label=component_id)
    for component_id in sorted_components
]
component_legend = ax4.legend(
    handles=component_legend_handles,
    title="Component",
    loc="upper left",
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1.0),
    fontsize=6,
    title_fontsize=7,
    ncol=2,
    frameon=False,
    labelcolor=TEXT_COLOR,
)
component_legend.get_title().set_color(TEXT_COLOR)

fig4.subplots_adjust(right=0.75)
plt.savefig(PER_QUERY_COUNT_BARPLOT_OUT, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
print(f"Saved per-query hit count bar plot to {PER_QUERY_COUNT_BARPLOT_OUT}")

# ─── PIE CHART: SHARE OF SIGNIFICANT HITS BY QUERY SEQUENCE (TOP N + OTHER) ─── #
plot_share_pie(
    ranked_hit_counts,
    TOP_N_QUERIES,
    label_for=lambda qseqid: f"{qseqid}\n{component_lookup.get(qseqid, '')}",
    color_for=lambda qseqid: component_color[component_lookup[qseqid]],
    title=f"Share of significant hits by query sequence\n(top {min(TOP_N_QUERIES, len(ranked_hit_counts)):,} of {len(ranked_hit_counts):,} query sequences, colored by component)",
    out_path=PER_QUERY_SHARE_PIE_OUT,
)

# ─── COMPONENT-LEVEL AGGREGATION: TOTAL SIGNIFICANT HITS PER COMPONENT ─── #
component_hit_counts = Counter()
for qseqid, count in hit_counts.items():
    component_hit_counts[component_lookup[qseqid]] += count
ranked_component_counts = component_hit_counts.most_common()  # [(component_id, count), ...] descending

component_labels = [component_id for component_id, count in ranked_component_counts]
component_counts = [count for component_id, count in ranked_component_counts]
component_bar_colors = [component_color[component_id] for component_id in component_labels]

# ─── BAR PLOT: SIGNIFICANT HIT COUNT PER COMPONENT (RANKED, LOG COUNT) ─── #
fig6, ax6 = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
ax6.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

ax6.bar(range(1, len(component_counts) + 1), component_counts, color=component_bar_colors, width=0.8, zorder=3)
ax6.set_yscale("log")

ax6.set_xticks(range(1, len(component_labels) + 1))
ax6.set_xticklabels(component_labels, rotation=90, fontsize=6, color=TEXT_COLOR)

ax6.set_xlabel("Component (ranked by significant hit count)", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax6.set_ylabel("Significant hits (log scale)", color=TEXT_COLOR)
ax6.set_title(f"Significant hits per component ({len(component_labels):,} components)", color=TEXT_COLOR)

ax6.tick_params(colors=TEXT_COLOR)
for spine in ax6.spines.values():
    spine.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
    spine.set_alpha(0.4)

ax6.grid(True, axis="y", color=TEXT_COLOR, alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5, zorder=0)
ax6.set_axisbelow(True)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(COMPONENT_COUNT_BARPLOT_OUT, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150)
plt.show()
print(f"Saved per-component hit count bar plot to {COMPONENT_COUNT_BARPLOT_OUT}")

# ─── PIE CHART: SHARE OF SIGNIFICANT HITS BY COMPONENT ─── #
fig7, ax7 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 10), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
ax7.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

wedges7, labels7, autotexts7 = ax7.pie(
    component_counts,
    labels=component_labels,
    colors=component_bar_colors,
    autopct="%1.1f%%",
    pctdistance=0.8,
    startangle=90,
    counterclock=False,
    wedgeprops={"edgecolor": BACKGROUND_COLOR, "linewidth": 1},
    textprops={"color": TEXT_COLOR, "fontsize": 6},
)
for autotext in autotexts7:
    autotext.set_color(BACKGROUND_COLOR)
    autotext.set_fontsize(5)
    autotext.set_fontweight("bold")

ax7.set_title(f"Share of significant hits by component ({len(component_labels):,} components)", color=TEXT_COLOR)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(COMPONENT_SHARE_PIE_OUT, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150)
plt.show()
print(f"Saved per-component hit share pie chart to {COMPONENT_SHARE_PIE_OUT}")

# ─── OVERALL PID AND E-VALUE HISTOGRAMS (ALL SIGNIFICANT HITS) ─── #
plot_pid_histogram(
    overall_pidents,
    f"%Identity distribution ({n_total_hits:,} significant hits)",
    ALL_PID_HISTOGRAM,
    show=True,
)
print(f"Saved overall PID histogram to {ALL_PID_HISTOGRAM}")

plot_eval_histogram(
    overall_evalues,
    f"E-value distribution ({n_total_hits:,} significant hits)",
    ALL_EVAL_HISTOGRAM,
    show=True,
)
print(f"Saved overall e-value histogram to {ALL_EVAL_HISTOGRAM}")

# ─── PER-QUERY PID AND E-VALUE HISTOGRAMS ─── #
os.makedirs(PER_QUERY_PID_HISTOGRAM_DIR, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(PER_QUERY_EVAL_HISTOGRAM_DIR, exist_ok=True)

n_plotted = 0
for qseqid, pidents in query_pidents.items():
    n_plotted += 1
    if n_plotted % 50 == 0:
        print(f"\rPlotted {n_plotted:,} / {len(query_pidents):,} per-query histograms", end="", flush=True)

    safe_qseqid = qseqid.replace("|", "_").replace("/", "_")
    n_query_hits = len(pidents)

    plot_pid_histogram(
        pidents,
        f"{qseqid}\n%identity distribution ({n_query_hits:,} significant hits)",
        os.path.join(PER_QUERY_PID_HISTOGRAM_DIR, f"{safe_qseqid}.png"),
    )
    plot_eval_histogram(
        query_evalues[qseqid],
        f"{qseqid}\nE-value distribution ({n_query_hits:,} significant hits)",
        os.path.join(PER_QUERY_EVAL_HISTOGRAM_DIR, f"{safe_qseqid}.png"),
    )

print(f"\rPlotted {n_plotted:,} / {len(query_pidents):,} per-query histograms")
print(f"Saved per-query PID histograms to {PER_QUERY_PID_HISTOGRAM_DIR}")
print(f"Saved per-query e-value histograms to {PER_QUERY_EVAL_HISTOGRAM_DIR}")
```

### 2.4. Search our old Plasticome set against NCBI nr
---
I want to compare the increase in the dataset now that we have the updated Plasticome.v2 query fastaa. Do we get more sequences, or was the doubling of Plasticome really just sampling the same sequence space as Plasticome.v1?


```bash
%%bash

# ───────────────────────────────────── #
# SEARCH PLASTICOME.V1 AGAINST NCBI NR  #
# ───────────────────────────────────── #

# ─── INPUT ─── #
PLASTICOME_V1_FASTAA="./2_nr_search/input/petadex-plasticome.v1.fastaa"
DIAMOND_NR_DATABASE="./2_nr_search/input/ncbi-blast_nr-2.17.0+.dmnd"

# ─── OUTPUT ─── #
NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH_V1="./2_nr_search/output/petadex-nr.v1.raw_hits.pro"

# ─── LOGS ─── #
DIAMOND_LOG_V1="./2_nr_search/logs/petadex-nr.v1.raw_hits.log"

# ─── WORKING DIRECTORY ─── #
TEMP_DIR="./2_nr_search/working/tmp"

# ─── PERFORM SEARCH ─── #
echo "Starting up Plasticome.v1 Search..."
diamond blastp \
  -d "${DIAMOND_NR_DATABASE}" \
  -q "${PLASTICOME_V1_FASTAA}" \
  -o "${NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH_V1}" \
  --very-sensitive \
  -k0 \
  -b140 \
  -c1 \
  --threads 120 \
  --tmpdir "${TEMP_DIR}" \
  --outfmt 6 qseqid sseqid pident length mismatch gapopen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore \
  > "${DIAMOND_LOG_V1}" 2>&1
cat "${DIAMOND_LOG_V1}"
```

### 2.5. Parse and plot the Plasticome.v1 results
---
This section will be a compressed version of sections 2.2 and 2.3 and 2.4. It will read the diamond output file and take the top e-value hit per sequence and the plot histograms of the e-values and pids of the entire set of sequences below the e-value cut-off. The only output files will be the plots, as I won't be using these hits anything further than this quick analysis.

It additionally creates a venn diagram of the hits from Plasticome.v1 and Plasticome.v2 to see how the sequence space is expanding.


```python
# ───────────── #
# SCRIPT SET UP #
# ───────────── #
print("Starting up...")

import csv
import math
from collections import Counter

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ─── INPUT ─── #
NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH_V1 = "./2_nr_search/output/petadex-nr.v1.raw_hits.pro"
FIELDS = ["qseqid","sseqid","pident","length","mismatch","gapopen","qstart","qend","sstart","send","evalue","bitscore"]

NR_CLEANED_TARGETS = "../s3/2_nr_search/petadex-nr.v260701.significant-hits.fastaa" # lacks plasticome
""" Format:
>genbank_accession,genbank_accession,ect|e_value|pid|bitscore|query_petadex_id|component_id
"""

# ─── OUTPUT ─── #
PID_HISTOGRAM_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v1.pid_histogram.png"
EVAL_HISTOGRAM_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v1.evalue_histogram.png"
PER_QUERY_SHARE_PIE_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v1.per_query_share_pie.png"
VENN_DIAGRAM_OUT = "./2_nr_search/images/petadex-nr.v1_v2.accession_overlap_venn.png"

# ─── PARAMETERS ─── #
EVALUE_CUTOFF = 1.0e-5
TOP_N_QUERIES = 20  # number of individual slices in the per-query share pie chart, rest folds into "Other"

# ─── PLOT STYLE (venn diagram only; histograms/pie reuse 2.3's style) ─── #
V1_CIRCLE_COLOR = PID_BIN_COLOR
V2_CIRCLE_COLOR = EVAL_BIN_COLOR

# ───────────────────── #
# CREATE PLOT FUNCTIONS #
# ───────────────────── #
"""
NOTE: The pid histogram, evalue histogram, pie plots and colour palette functions are in 2.3.
"""

def pct_of_total(n, n_total):
    return f"{n / n_total * 100:.1f}%" if n_total else "0.0%"

def plot_venn_diagram(n_v1_only, n_v2_only_groups, n_shared_groups, n_v1_total, n_v2_total, out_path):
    """
    Plots a venn diagram comparing the sequences found in
    Plasticome.v1 to Plasticome.v2. The radius of the circles
    are scaled by sqrt of the circle sequence count.
    """
    n_total_for_pct = n_v1_only + n_v2_only_groups + n_shared_groups

    r1 = math.sqrt(n_v1_total)
    r2 = math.sqrt(n_v2_total)
    scale = 3.2 / max(r1, r2)
    r1 *= scale
    r2 *= scale

    center_distance = (r1 + r2) * 0.55
    c1_x, c2_x = -center_distance / 2, center_distance / 2

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 7), facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR)
    ax.set_facecolor(BACKGROUND_COLOR)

    circle1 = plt.Circle((c1_x, 0), r1, color=V1_CIRCLE_COLOR, alpha=0.55, zorder=2, linewidth=0)
    circle2 = plt.Circle((c2_x, 0), r2, color=V2_CIRCLE_COLOR, alpha=0.55, zorder=2, linewidth=0)
    ax.add_patch(circle1)
    ax.add_patch(circle2)

    ax.text(c1_x - r1 * 0.45, 0, f"{n_v1_only:,}\n({pct_of_total(n_v1_only, n_total_for_pct)})",
             ha="center", va="center", color=TEXT_COLOR, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    ax.text(c2_x + r2 * 0.45, 0, f"{n_v2_only_groups:,}\n({pct_of_total(n_v2_only_groups, n_total_for_pct)})",
             ha="center", va="center", color=TEXT_COLOR, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    ax.text(0, 0, f"{n_shared_groups:,}\n({pct_of_total(n_shared_groups, n_total_for_pct)})",
             ha="center", va="center", color=BACKGROUND_COLOR, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")

    ax.text(c1_x, r1 + 0.4, "Plasticome.v1\n(non-redundant groups)", ha="center", va="bottom", color=V1_CIRCLE_COLOR, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
    ax.text(c2_x, r2 + 0.4, "Plasticome.v2\n(non-redundant groups)", ha="center", va="bottom", color=V2_CIRCLE_COLOR, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")

    ax.set_xlim(c1_x - r1 * 1.3, c2_x + r2 * 1.3)
    ax.set_ylim(-max(r1, r2) * 1.5, max(r1, r2) * 1.7)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")

    ax.set_title(
        f"Overlap of significant-hit groups\nPlasticome.v1 ({n_v1_total:,} non-redundant groups) vs Plasticome.v2 ({n_v2_total:,} non-redundant groups)",
        color=TEXT_COLOR,
    )

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_path, facecolor=BACKGROUND_COLOR, dpi=150)
    plt.show()
    print(f"Saved accession overlap venn diagram to {out_path}")

# ───────────────────────────────── #
# PARSE PLASTICOME V1 SEARCH OUTPUT #
# ───────────────────────────────── #
n_total_hits = 0
best_hit = {}  # sseqid -> (pident, evalue, qseqid) of the lowest-evalue hit
with open(NCBI_OUTPUT_SEARCH_V1) as diamond_output:
    reader = csv.DictReader(diamond_output, delimiter="\t", fieldnames=FIELDS)
    for row in reader:
        n_total_hits += 1
        sequence_id = row["sseqid"]
        pident = float(row["pident"])
        evalue = float(row["evalue"])
        qseqid = row["qseqid"]

        if sequence_id not in best_hit or evalue < best_hit[sequence_id][1]:
            best_hit[sequence_id] = (pident, evalue, qseqid)

print(f"Total hits in DIAMOND output: {n_total_hits:,}")
print(f"Unique target sequences:     {len(best_hit):,}")

# ─── ENFORCE E-VALUE CUTOFF ─── #
passing_hits = {
    sequence_id: (pident, evalue, qseqid)
    for sequence_id, (pident, evalue, qseqid) in best_hit.items()
    if evalue <= EVALUE_CUTOFF
}
passing_pidents = [pident for pident, evalue, qseqid in passing_hits.values()]
passing_evalues = [evalue for pident, evalue, qseqid in passing_hits.values()]
print(f"Sequences passing e-value cutoff (<= {EVALUE_CUTOFF:g}): {len(passing_hits):,} / {len(best_hit):,}")

# ──────────────────────── #
# CREATE PLOTS FOR V1 ONLY #
# ──────────────────────── #
plot_pid_histogram(
    passing_pidents,
    f"Plasticome.v1: %identity distribution ({len(passing_pidents):,} groups below {EVALUE_CUTOFF:g})",
    PID_HISTOGRAM_OUT,
    show=True,
)
print(f"Saved PID histogram to {PID_HISTOGRAM_OUT}")

plot_eval_histogram(
    passing_evalues,
    f"Plasticome.v1: E-value distribution ({len(passing_evalues):,} groups below {EVALUE_CUTOFF:g})",
    EVAL_HISTOGRAM_OUT,
    show=True,
)
print(f"Saved e-value histogram to {EVAL_HISTOGRAM_OUT}")

# ─── PIE CHART: SHARE OF SIGNIFICANT HITS BY QUERY SEQUENCE (TOP N + OTHER) ─── #
query_hit_counts = Counter()
for pident, evalue, qseqid in passing_hits.values():
    query_hit_counts[qseqid] += 1
ranked_query_hit_counts = query_hit_counts.most_common()  # [(qseqid, count), ...] descending by count
print(f"Unique query sequences with a passing hit: {len(ranked_query_hit_counts):,}")

plot_share_pie(
    ranked_query_hit_counts,
    TOP_N_QUERIES,
    label_for=lambda qseqid: qseqid,
    title=f"Plasticome.v1: share of significant hits by query sequence\n(top {min(TOP_N_QUERIES, len(ranked_query_hit_counts)):,} of {len(ranked_query_hit_counts):,} query sequences)",
    out_path=PER_QUERY_SHARE_PIE_OUT,
)

# ───────────────────────────────── #
# PARSE PLASTICOME V2 SEARCH OUTPUT #
# ───────────────────────────────── #
def iter_headers(path):
    with open(path) as fasta:
        for line in fasta:
            if line.startswith(">"):
                yield line.rstrip("\n")[1:]

v2_groups = []  # [(accessions, qseqid), ...] one entry per header, index = group_id
v2_accession_to_group = {}  # genbank_accession -> group_id, for every redundant copy

n_v2_headers = 0
for header in iter_headers(NR_CLEANED_TARGETS):
    n_v2_headers += 1
    if n_v2_headers % 500_000 == 0:
        print(f"\rParsed {n_v2_headers:,} Plasticome.v2 significant-hit headers", end="", flush=True)

    # the accessions field (first field) can itself contain "|" characters from
    # legacy NCBI header formats, so split from the right for the 5 known
    # trailing fields instead of splitting on every "|" in the header
    fields = header.rsplit("|", 5)
    qseqid = fields[4]
    accessions = fields[0].split(",")  # all redundant accessions for this one non-redundant sequence

    group_id = len(v2_groups)
    v2_groups.append((accessions, qseqid))
    for accession in accessions:
        v2_accession_to_group[accession] = group_id

print(f"\rParsed {n_v2_headers:,} Plasticome.v2 significant-hit headers")
print(f"Non-redundant Plasticome.v2 groups (sequences): {len(v2_groups):,}")
print(f"Total Plasticome.v2 accessions (incl. redundant copies): {len(v2_accession_to_group):,}")

# ───────────────────────── #
# PARSE OVERLAP OF V1 VS V2 #
# ───────────────────────── #

# ─── GETS COUNT OF ACCESSIONS IN PLASTICOME V1 THAT MATCH TO ANY ACCESSION IN V2 ─── #
v1_sequence_ids = set(passing_hits.keys())

shared_group_ids = set()
v1_matched_sequence_ids = set()
for sequence_id in v1_sequence_ids:
    group_id = v2_accession_to_group.get(sequence_id)
    if group_id is not None:
        shared_group_ids.add(group_id)
        v1_matched_sequence_ids.add(sequence_id)

n_v2_groups = len(v2_groups)
n_shared_groups = len(shared_group_ids)
n_v2_only_groups = n_v2_groups - n_shared_groups
n_v1_only = len(v1_sequence_ids) - len(v1_matched_sequence_ids)

print(f"Plasticome.v1 significant-hit sequences:              {len(v1_sequence_ids):,}")
print(f"Plasticome.v2 significant-hit sequences:              {n_v2_groups:,}")
print(f"Shared sequences:                                     {n_shared_groups:,}")
print(f"Groups unique to Plasticome.v2:                       {n_v2_only_groups:,}")
print(f"Sequences unique to Plasticome.v1:                    {n_v1_only:,}")

# ───────────────────── #
# CREATE OVERLAP PLOTS  #
# ───────────────────── #
plot_venn_diagram(n_v1_only, n_v2_only_groups, n_shared_groups, len(v1_sequence_ids), n_v2_groups, VENN_DIAGRAM_OUT)

# ─── COUNT OF SEQUENCES (V1) / SEQUENCES (V2) PER QUERY ─── #
v1_only_sequence_ids = v1_sequence_ids - v1_matched_sequence_ids
v1_only_query_counts = Counter(passing_hits[sequence_id][2] for sequence_id in v1_only_sequence_ids)

v2_only_query_counts = Counter()
n_v2_only_accessions = 0
for group_id, (accessions, qseqid) in enumerate(v2_groups):
    if group_id in shared_group_ids:
        continue
    n_v2_only_accessions += len(accessions)
    v2_only_query_counts[qseqid] += len(accessions)
```

## 3. Summary of Results
### 3.1 Raw Hits
---
We retrieved a total of 42,053,081 hits through this search, which after removing redundant hits (many query to one target), we have 8,850,583 unique amino acid sequences hit (no e-value cutoff).

Overall, as you can see, a million hits do not meet the e-value cutoff, which I think makes sense. As you incrementally decrease the e-value cutoff, you retrieve less and less sequences, but there are still a lot of hits even when you go to e-values like 1.0e-30 (2.8 million). This data doesn't look strange to me.

### 3.2 Parsed Hits
---
Overall, after applying an e-value cut-off of 1.0E-5, you recieve 7,825,107 amino acid sequence hits. This encompasses 13,209,543 unique GenBank accessions.

### 3.3. Parsed Hits per Component
---
Most components have about 10,000 to 100,000 homologs in nr, so the hits per components are relatively spread out.

There are a few high hitting components:
- C16 = Cytochrome homologs. This makes a ton of sense since this is a very, very well studied protein within all kingdoms of life (in humans!), These are oxygenases and are the main enzyme in drug metabolism, so they have evolved to be able to break down almost everything.
- C3 = amidases which break down N-C bonds. We don't have many components of amidases so it makes sense that this one grabs a ton of sequences
- C34 = these are a group of ab hydrolases - carboxylesterases?. I don't really know why there is so many of these puppy dogs.
- C14 = another set of ab hydrolases -- esterases? Also can't tell you why there is so many

But overall it seems that 75% of our database can be attributed to just 8 components.

There are a few very low hit components:
- C39 = singleton PLA depolymerase
- C33 = singleton archeaic PETase
- C23 = singleton unknown carboxylesterase
- C27 = singleton PLA depolymerase from the same paper as C39

It would be cool to see how many more hits we can get out of Logan of these understudied guys.

C1 is IsPETase homologs, such as LCC, and it represents a lot of hits which is very good if we want to deep dive investigate that component some more.

### 3.4. Parsed Hits per Query
---
Some of the query sequences form most of the hits per each component which is interesting, and some of the query sequences are most of the dataset, as just 3 sequences represent 25% of the total diamond output:
- PL175 (cytochrome P450 singleton cluster)
- PL128 (DD-peptidase singleton cluster)
- PL109 (urethanase amidase - non-singleton).

As you can see, the top two are singletons, so perhaps if there were more sequences in that component the hits would be more split across the component, such as with component 1.

Just 11 sequences represents 50% of our total hits, so the dataset is not as distributed equally as I would have thought or have liked.

One of the query sequences had no hits (PL411). When looking at the top hits for these sequence on BLAST, you find that the top 5 are either Plasticome sequences, or hit to Plasticome sequences. When looking at the raw hits, PL411 does in have hits, but they are always higher e-value than another sequence, therefore is not attributed the hit.

### 3.5. Final Stats of Significant Hits
---
There is a normal-ish distribution of pid values around 30%, so it shows that most of the nr dataset iis from new superfamilies. This follows with the previous search I believe.

The e-value makes sense, and seems to follow an exponential increase of hits as the e-value decreases.


### 3.6. Hits per query sequence
---
Here's the number of hits per query sequence in a table format. The following is Dennis' seed set for centroids and their hits:
- IsPETase has 71 hits
- LCC has 56 hits
- TfCut_2 has 60
- Cut190 has 45
- HiC has 52
- Mipa-P has 24
- Kuba-P has 7
- NylA has 10723
- NylB has 40806
- NylC has 147
- PhaZ1 has 19259
- PLAse I has 2843
- PueA has 5344
- PET6 has 25

Overall, it seems that the main studied AB hydrolases have relatively low hits within the dataset / their hits are being absorbed by other sequences in their component. There are a few sequences that take up the majority of the dataset.

### 3.7. Comparison to Plasticome.v1
---
